name: TotalSegmentator OsiriX/Horos Plugin
summary: Run TotalSegmentator segmentation from an OsiriX or Horos imaging workflow.
intro: Export an image series to a local segmentation workflow and import supported results back into the viewer. Configure the task, device and output location using the plugin's native controls.

features.title: Native workflow
features.body: Launch segmentation from OsiriX or Horos and inspect supported ROI results.

features.title: Task controls
features.body: Choose available tasks, device settings, fast mode and supported region subsets.

features.title: Environment setup
features.body: Check a Python runtime and conversion tools or prepare a managed environment.

features.title: Run artifacts
features.body: Keep segmentation outputs and provenance records for review.

support.title: Prepare the host
paragraphs: Install the plugin for a supported OsiriX or Horos environment and follow the repository’s build and installation instructions. Host compatibility and ROI behavior require validation in the actual viewer.

support.title: Check dependencies
paragraphs: Use environment checks to verify Python, TotalSegmentator and dcm2niix. Managed setup installs pinned Python dependencies and may download a conversion binary.

support.title: Run a segmentation
paragraphs: Select an appropriate series, choose a supported task and output directory, and review device and license requirements. Model weights may need downloading before the first run.

support.title: Review results and failures
paragraphs: Inspect the progress log and output/provenance records when a run fails. Verify imported segmentation alignment and completeness against the source images; successful processing is not clinical validation.

support.title: Review usage reporting
paragraphs: For the inspected Python library, usage reporting is controlled by send_usage_stats in config.json, normally in the .totalsegmentator directory under the user home. Set it to false to disable usage-report requests, and verify the directory and behavior for the runtime selected by the plugin. No native telemetry toggle was identified.

privacy.title: Local series processing
paragraphs: The plugin exports source image data for a local Python segmentation process and imports supported outputs into the host viewer. Source data, derived masks and run artifacts can contain sensitive information.

privacy.title: Dependencies and models
paragraphs: Environment preparation uses package downloads and may retrieve dcm2niix from GitHub. TotalSegmentator downloads missing model weights; some tasks require a license and contact its backend.

privacy.title: TotalSegmentator telemetry
paragraphs: The bundled Python library creates configuration with send_usage_stats enabled by default. Its usage request contains an installation identifier, run counter, task/options, platform and Python/GPU information, and a license number when present. The inspected request does not include image pixels or patient tags and uses an HTTP backend endpoint.

In the inspected library, setting send_usage_stats to false in its config.json disables these usage-report requests. Check the configuration directory used by your installed runtime; this setting does not disable model downloads or license-related requests.

privacy.title: Installed runtime matters
paragraphs: The plugin can use an installed Python environment or prepare one with pinned packages. Network and telemetry behavior must be checked in that actual TotalSegmentator version and its configuration; the native plugin does not establish a blanket offline or no-collection guarantee.

privacy.title: Stored settings and outputs
paragraphs: Plugin preferences, including an optional license key, are stored in macOS user defaults in the inspected code. Output directories retain segmentation and provenance artifacts, and progress logs can contain local paths. The host viewer manages its own database and ROI persistence.

privacy.title: Cleanup and deletion
paragraphs: The plugin includes temporary-export cleanup and staging cleanup, but completed outputs and host records have separate lifecycles. Review remaining output directories, logs, backups and viewer records when removing a case; no universal automatic deletion period is specified.
